title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Euler's sorting of expressions built from a curve y = y(x) into three kinds. That sorting prepares his 'new and easy' reformulation of the calculus of variations, which comes on the following pages.

The three kinds:
(i) Ordinary functions of x and y, such as αx³+βxy+γy³ or e^{αx} arcsin y. These are on the previous page.
(ii) Functions that also involve ratios of differentials of any order. With dy = p dx, dp = q dx, dq = r dx, and so on, these are functions of (x, y, p, q, r, …). In modern terms they are functions on the jet space, F(x, y, y', y'', …).
(iii) Integral formulas ∫V dx, where V depends on x, y, p, q, r, …. V may itself contain further integral formulas, so nested functionals of the type ∫V(x, y, p, ∫W dx) dx are included.

Section 3 states the problem of the calculus of variations. Replace the relation y(x) by another relation that differs from it infinitely little but otherwise arbitrarily. Then find the resulting change in every expression of all three kinds.

Euler recalls his earlier method. Besides the ordinary differential dy, which is the change of y when x becomes x+dx, y receives a second increment δy. This increment is wholly arbitrary and not determined by x, and he called it the 'variation'. The next page announces the reform. y is to be regarded as a function of two variables y(x,t), for example y = X + tV, so that δy = dt·∂y/∂t. The calculus of variations thus reduces to the second part of the integral calculus, the calculus of functions of two variables. This is the modern one-parameter family of variations, with first variation (d/dt)|_{t=0}.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. It is expository: definitions and a statement of the problem only.

ideas.what: Three-way sorting of expressions: point functions f(x,y); functions of the derivatives p, q, r, …; integral functionals ∫V dx, possibly nested
ideas.modern_name: Functions on jet space vs. functionals; nested (non-local) integral functionals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Methodus inveniendi 1744 for p, q, r notation and nested-integral functionals); Lagrange 1760s for δ-notation
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (E65, 1744), esp. ch. 3 on formulas containing integrals; Elementa calculi variationum (E296); Institutiones calculi integralis vol. III appendix

ideas.what: Variation δy as an arbitrary infinitesimal increment independent of dx, alongside the ordinary differential dy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1755 letter, 1762 paper); adopted and named 'variation' by Euler (E296, 1766)
ideas.where_published: E296 Elementa calculi variationum; E297 Analytica explicatio methodi maximorum et minimorum

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely introductory recap of Euler's earlier variational setup. The genuinely interesting step, the two-variable reformulation y(x,t), comes on the next page and is well documented in the histories of the calculus of variations.
transcription_corrections: Page number reads '36' (journal pagination, Novi Commentarii 16), not '382'.
'a ieo' should read 'adeo' ('quam rationem adeo ad differentialia cuiusque gradus extendimus').
Long-s forms in the original (e.g. 'expreſſionum') are normalized to 's' in the given transcription; content is unaffected.
